# Sync contacts across systems: PostgreSQL

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers integrations work end to end across PostgreSQL and HubSpot.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Pull Side A (HubSpot)
3. Pull Side B (PostgreSQL)
4. Diff the Two Systems
5. Create Missing in PostgreSQL
6. Count In-Sync Rows
7. Apply Updates to PostgreSQL
8. Backfill into HubSpot
9. Gather Sync Results

## Why it exists

Doing integrations work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Pull Side A (HubSpot) → Pull Side B (PostgreSQL) → Diff the Two Systems → Create Missing in PostgreSQL → Count In-Sync Rows → Apply Updates to PostgreSQL → Backfill into HubSpot → Gather Sync Results

## Use it for

- Teams keeping PostgreSQL and HubSpot aligned by hand for integrations
- Reconciling PostgreSQL against HubSpot after the two quietly drifted apart
- Integrations work where "Pull Side A (HubSpot)" is still a manual step before PostgreSQL
- Integrations work that only reaches PostgreSQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps PostgreSQL and HubSpot in step for integrations, without anyone re-typing a row
- Compares PostgreSQL against HubSpot before writing, so only genuine differences land
- A failed PostgreSQL or HubSpot call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this integrations build
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for integrations before wiring PostgreSQL
- 9 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for integrations

## Before first run
Connect credentials: HubSpot private-app token; Postgres connection.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Compare Datasets does the matching instead of hand-rolled join logic — one node produces four labeled lanes (only-in-A, matching, different, only-in-B), and each lane gets exactly the action it needs (create / count / update / backfill) instead of one generic 'sync' branch trying to cover every case.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Swap Side A or Side B for a third platform and rewire the merge-by-fields key.
2. Intentionally create a mismatch between the two systems and trace which lane it lands in.
3. Change mergeByFields to a different key and see how the diff results shift.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your integrations process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole integrations payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
